## The Onsen and its sauna

2 rows, each painted twice: the two rooms inside the hot-spring house on your Mountain Path, its rest hall with the spring outside, and the sauna. Nobody is in either picture.

Run this in the **local ComfyUI**. Press **Run** once.

Each row is one picture, painted twice: **version A** on top, **version B** under it. You choose between them afterwards.

The **Load Image** boxes on the left should already show their pictures. If one shows an error, click **choose file to upload** and pick the file with the same name from `JJK Game images/ui2/early`.

**Cost:** 4 pictures, about **$0.64** (Nano Banana Pro, about $0.16 a picture, charged to your Comfy account).

You don't need to save anything: the results go to ComfyUI's output folder and Claude picks them up from there.

If it stops with a rate-limit or "high demand" error, wait a minute and press **Run** again: a finished picture is reused, not paid for twice (as long as ComfyUI hasn't been restarted).

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel: a new picture of one room of a traditional Japanese mountain school, built of timber and white plaster. Picture 1 is the mountain path this room's building stands on, already painted: the same school. Picture 2 is this room's own building, cut from picture 1 and seen from outside: the timber house with the grey tiled roof, its entrance under a small canopy with a dark-blue door curtain, and beside it the fence of wooden planks with steam rising behind. The new picture is the inside of that house. Do not copy the camera or the layout of either picture: the new picture is taken indoors, and it shows the room, not the outside of the building. THE PLACE: the inside of the hot-spring house of picture 2: its rest hall. It is a calm, airy hall of pale timber and white plaster, about ten metres long and six wide, with a floor of smooth timber boards and a ceiling of dark beams. I stand inside at one end and look along the hall. The right wall is the front of the house seen from inside: halfway along it the entrance, a wide sliding timber door, stands open under the short dark-blue door curtain of picture 2, and through it I see the stone basin that stands by the door, the grass and earth of the mountain path, and tall cedars beyond; the stretch of the right wall nearest me is plain plaster. The far end of the hall has no wall: its paper screens are slid wide open onto the hot spring outside, a pool edged with rounded grey stones, its water still and steaming and quite empty, closed round by the tall fence of wooden planks of picture 2, with the tops of cedars and a green mountain slope above the fence. On the left wall, a little way along, stands a small glass-fronted fridge with rows of small milk bottles in it; further along the left wall is a plain door of cedar boards, shut, with no window in it. A standing electric fan stands in the far left corner, and low timber benches run along the walls. The hall is empty and tidy. The floor is clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. The picture is seen from standing eye height, the horizon a little above the middle. Leave the right ninth of the picture and the top-left corner free of doors, shelves and anything else one would walk to or use. THE LOOK: a real place you could walk into, drawn as a clean modern anime background. Believable materials (wood grain, glass with soft reflections, stone, plaster, fabric), physically believable light with soft shadows and bounced light, real depth. Clean and well kept: walls are fresh and even, with no stains, cracks, peeling, damp patches or dirt, and there is no dust, litter or fallen leaves on the floor or the ground; everything that belongs to the place is still there. Crisp precise edges, clean clear colour, no film grain, no noise, no canvas texture, no visible brush strokes, no haze or glow washing out detail. Through every window a clear, in-focus view. No people, no animals, no text, no logos. Output a 16:9 picture.

Picture 1 is the house this room is inside, cut from a picture already painted and seen from outside: the same school, the same timber. The new picture is taken indoors, in a small room at the back of that house that has no window, and it shows nothing of the outside. Do not copy its camera or its layout. THE PLACE: the inside of the sauna of the hot-spring house of picture 1: a small room with no window, lined from floor to ceiling with pale cedar boards, about three metres wide and four long, lit only by the warm orange light of its own stove. I stand at the back of the room and look toward its door. In the far wall, left of the middle, is the door, of plain cedar boards, shut, with no window in it. Beside the door, to its right, stands a round tub of grey stone, knee high, filled with clear still water and quite empty, with a bamboo spout above it from which a thin stream of water falls into the tub. Along the left wall runs a bench of cedar boards in a lower and an upper step, plain and empty. Against the right wall, halfway along and well clear of the picture's right edge, stands the stove: a low black iron stove with a heap of dark round stones on top, its fire showing orange through a small grate; on the floor beside it stand a wooden bucket of water and a long wooden ladle. The floor is cedar boards, clear and empty. The stove's fire is the only light: it lies warm on the boards near it and leaves the far corners dim, but everything in the room can still be seen clearly. The picture is seen from standing eye height, the horizon a little above the middle.
